1.

By way of present petition filed under Section 378 (3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 the State has sought leave to appeal against the impugned judgment of acquittal dated 23.12.2022 passed by the learned Special Additional Sessions Judge, Pendraroad, District-Bilaspur (Now State Of Chhattisgarh vs Pawan Kumar Rathore on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102072867/
1 Gourela-Pendra-Marwahi) (C.G.) in Special Sessions Trial No. 15/2021 by which the respondent/accused has been acquitted of the charges punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 (3)
of Indian Penal Code and under Section 4 read with Section 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and under Sections 3 (2) (v), 3 (1) (b) (1) of the Schedule Caste & Schedule Tribes (Prevention of Atrocity Act, 1989) by giving the benefit of doubt.

sentences.text: 2. I.A. No. 01/2023, is an application for condonation of delay of 23 days in filing the instant petition for leave to appeal.
3. For the reasons mentioned in the application, the same is allowed.
Delay in filing the petition for leave to appeal is condoned.

4. It has been argued by learned State counsel that the learned trial Court has disbelieved the evidence of the prosecution witnesses and has acquitted the accused / respondent from the charges leveled against him.

It is also stated that no doubt there was dispute between the brother of the victim and the accused / respondent and the instant FIR has been lodged against the accused /
respondent under Sections 363 & 373 of IPC and under Section 4 read with Section 6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and thereafter the final report is submitted on 23.11.2020 before the concerned criminal Court wherein the appellant has also been convicted under Section 3 (2) (v) of the Schedule Caste and Schedule Tribe (Prevention of Atrocity Act, 1989).

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Schedule Caste and Schedule Tribe (Prevention of Atrocity Act, 1989)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
It is also stated that the victim as well as the brother of the victim have supported the case of the prosecution and moreover the same is also corroborated by the MLC vide Ex. 18A & 18 and FSL report vide Ex.P/33.
5.
In view of above, we are of the considered opinion that the present is a fit case where application under Section 378 (3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 deserves to be allowed.

Accordingly,
the application for leave to appeal under Section 378 (3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 is allowed.

6. Office is directed to register the case under the head of "Acquittal Appeal".
7.
The CrMP is disposed of accordingly.
8. The Acquittal Appeal also stands admitted.

9. Let a bailable warrant for a sum of Rs. 5,000/- be issued against the respondent / accused for his presence before this Court on 22nd January, 2025 through concerned Chief Judicial Magistrate.
10.

List the Acquittal Appeal on 22nd January, 2025.
 Sd/- Sd/-
 (Amitendra Kishore Prasad) (Ramesh Sinha)
